text.en: Rishi from Jammu is going on a bus to the Himalayas with his parents to visit his Mama, Mami and cousins Chiya and Nonikaa. On the way and at the village he sees hills covered with flowers, learns about tulips and the spring festivals of different places, and learns how to stay safe on the road.

Rishi is travelling by bus with his parents to a small village near the mountains, where his Mama (mother's brother), Mami (Mama's wife) and his cousins Chiya and Nonikaa live. He enjoys the bus ride. The roads have hairpin turns, the hills are covered with colourful flowers, and he can see tall trees far away. On the road we see many signboards, such as No Parking, No Horn Please, Speed Breaker, No U-Turn, Men at Work and School Ahead. Each board gives a message that keeps us safe. We should follow road signs and signals. We can draw and label signboards of our own, such as for the library, toilet, assembly, drinking water point, playground, stairs and our classroom.
They get down at the bus stop near the village and Mamaji is there to receive them. They walk on a broad concrete road that later becomes a narrow mud road near the house. At the gate Rishi sees a row of colourful flowers in the garden. He can name a rose, a marigold and a hibiscus, but he is amazed by one flower unlike any he has seen. He asks his cousin Nonikaa the name of the flower, and she says it is a tulip. Roads can be of different kinds: broad concrete roads, narrow mud roads, and winding hill roads. They change with the place.
Mami calls the children in for lunch. They eat a Kashmiri dish called haakh, a kind of leafy vegetable, with hot rice, and it is delicious. Nonikaa says that there is a Kashmir tulip festival at this time of the year. A festival can celebrate a flower, a season or a good crop. The food of different places is different. Haakh with rice is special to Kashmir, and we can ask our elders about the special food of our own place.
Rishi says that red flowers called buransh (rhododendron) bloom in spring in his place. On the spring festival there, people place mustard and buransh flowers at the doorstep of every home in the neighbourhood, and the elders bless the children and give them toffees and sweets. Chiya says her friend Unni from Kerala celebrates Vishu at this time of the year. They use yellow amaltas flowers, fruits and vegetables to make Vishu Kani. Vishu Kani is an auspicious sight seen at sunrise on the first day of the Malayali new year, and it is supposed to bring a fruitful year. Mami says spring is a celebration of nature. After the harsh winter the sun shines brightly, flowers bloom, the grass grows and the trees get new leaves. In Jharkhand, people celebrate Sarhul in spring. They wear traditional clothes and walk in a procession to the sakhua tree with sakhua flowers and freshly germinated grains. They make offerings to the Earth and the Sun and sing and dance to drums such as the dhol and nagada.
There are different seasons: spring, summer, monsoon and winter, and each has festivals of its own. Each festival has special food, such as thekua for Chhath Puja, pitha for Bihu, plum cake for Christmas, gujiya for Holi, sadya for Onam, holige for Ugadi and seviyan for Eid-ul-Fitr. We wear special clothes on festivals, and the clothes differ from place to place and from family to family. Not everybody eats the same special food or wears new clothes on festivals, and we should be sensitive to everyone.
Festivals bring families, friends and neighbours together. We meet relatives, share sweets, sing and dance. When we celebrate with people of other places and communities we learn new customs, foods and songs. Spring is a time of happiness. Children sing, 'Spring is in the air, happy children are everywhere'. We can spend time in nature, in the mountains, near rivers and streams, and feel happy there.
Gopu's and Rishi's stories take place in the north of India, where the most majestic mountains in the world lie. These mountains are called the Himalayas, which means the 'home of snow'. The highest peak in the world, Mount Everest, lies in our neighbouring country Nepal, and its height is about 8,848 metres.
Have you ever travelled in a bus? Share the experience with your classmates, and say what trees and flowers you saw on the way. Think about safety: what should you do while travelling in a bus, while riding a bicycle and while walking on the road? We use different modes of transport when we travel, such as buses, trains, cars, cycles and boats, and each needs its own safety rules.
Match the signboards in Column A with their meanings: No Parking, No Horn Please, Speed Breaker, No U-Turn, Men at Work and School Ahead. Draw and label any three more road signboards that were not on the list, so that you remember what they mean.
Sing the spring song together: Spring is in the air, happy children are everywhere, new leaves appear on the trees, as flowers sway in the breeze. Ask your elders the names of the festivals celebrated in your locality in spring, summer, monsoon and winter, and list the special food of each. Tell your classmates what special dresses you wear during festivals.
Do you think everyone celebrates festivals with special food and new clothes? We should remember that some families cannot, and we should be kind. Are there mountains, rivers or streams close to where you live, and how does it feel to visit relatives in a faraway place? Fill in the blanks: Chiya and Nonikaa live in a village near the mountains, and the red flowers of spring are called buransh. Name two relatives you visited recently, and tell how you spend time with your cousins.

problem.en: Draw a signboard for the school library.

text.en: Decide the message: Silence, please, or Library.

why.en: A sign needs a short message.

text.en: Choose a simple picture, like an open book, and bright colours.

why.en: Pictures are easy to understand quickly.

text.en: Draw it on chart paper and explain it to the class.

why.en: Explaining checks that others can understand it.

prompt.en: Tell a friend about a spring festival, and the food and clothes on festivals, and why festivals are special.

requiredIdeas.en: Spring is a season when flowers bloom and festivals like Sarhul and Vishu are celebrated
Each place and festival has special food and clothes

commonMisconceptions.en: Festivals are celebrated in the same way everywhere
Everyone eats the same food on festivals

points.en: Spring is a celebration of nature when flowers bloom and new leaves come out.
Festivals are celebrated differently in different places, such as the Tulip festival, Vishu and Sarhul.
Each festival has special food and clothes.
Road signboards keep us safe when we travel.
Festivals bring families, friends and neighbours together.
The Himalayas are the 'home of snow' and Mount Everest, about 8,848 metres, is the highest peak.
Sarhul in Jharkhand is celebrated with sakhua flowers, a procession, offerings to the Earth and the Sun, and drums.
We should be kind to families who cannot afford special food or new clothes.
